updates.problem: Atomic scientific claims could reference source strings without a fail-closed exact source snapshot/span identity contract, allowing stale versions, repeated passages or post-hoc locators to masquerade as grounded evidence.
updates.result: A frozen source SHA-256 plus exact code-point span/prefix/suffix locator now validates claim-evidence identity separately from an externally supplied semantic review record. Locator fidelity cannot establish semantic support, and neither layer grants scientific/target authority.
updates.remaining_gap: Automatic claim extraction, semantic relation validation, multi-span aggregation and real scientific utility are untested. Run a matched real claim-evidence benchmark before requiring this representation in generator/gluing/bridge workflows.
updates.falsifier: If exact-span provenance does not reduce stale/wrong-source errors or improve failure localization relative to source-level citation baselines, retain it as optional audit metadata rather than mandatory decision-layer complexity.

updates.note: Future real generator packets should bind generator-support claims to exact source/span provenance where available, while separately scoring semantic relation accuracy and evidence-lineage dependence.
Future multi-paper gluing packets should expose exact evidence spans behind transition/compatibility claims so locator failures can be distinguished from semantic or gluing failures.
Future bridge packets should distinguish exact span identity, semantic relation, path composition and target authority at every hop.
A deterministic compiler remains needed to reconstruct all fiber definitions/statuses and detect orphan/conflicting references.

saturation.reason: Round 030 retained a new exact claim-to-source-span provenance contract plus locator/semantic/authority separation after semantic deduplication.
